data.title: Ledger expands hardware hack investigation to Germany, UAE as new cases emerge
data.description:
Crypto hardware wallet maker Ledger has expanded its investigation into a physical supply-chain tampering campaign to Germany and the United Arab Emirates after identifying suspicious devices in Berlin and receiving loss reports in Dubai.

In a Wednesday update, the company said newly emerged cases were "the same incident" as ones involving tampered devices in Southeast Asia. It explained that it has confirmed the same kind of physical modification designed to capture the recovery phrase during setup.

"There is no flaw in Ledger's secure chip or operating system, and no confirmed case involving a device bought on ledger.com," Ledger stated in its update.

Ledger noted that it has progressed its investigation into reports of "a few tampered units" localized to Berlin, and urged anyone who purchased a device in the city from January to reach out to its support team.

In the UAE, the team has received reports of two tampered units in Dubai, and is investigating how they entered circulation. The company has also identified one case involving a newer model, the Ledger Nano Gen5, which was impacted in Southeast Asia.

Two X users, Rewinskyx and newbabylonorder, claimed to have lost a combined $604,000 in crypto from devices purchased at an authorized reseller in Dubai. The former reported losing about 1,300 SOL (SOL), while the latter said 507,000 USDT (USDT) was drained.

On Wednesday, Bitquery reported that roughly $1.68 million was stolen from 16 wallets in Dubai and Berlin, following the blockchain analytics firm's claim last month that the campaign drained about $102 million from 335 wallets in Southeast Asia.

Ledger has not officially confirmed the amount of losses from the supply chain tampering. The Block has reached out to Ledger for comment.

Origin

The expanded probe follows an investigation that began last month in Southeast Asia, where Ledger users reported unauthorized cryptocurrency drains. It was later identified that customers of authorized reseller CryptoBilis were targeted.

In a previous disclosure, Ledger stated that threat actors acquired genuine devices, installed additional custom-built hardware components to transmit recovery phrases externally, and reintroduced the units into reseller channels.

"As we continue our investigation, we expect it is possible that additional devices will be found, and we are working with partners and authorities to find affected devices as quickly as possible," Ledger said in the latest update. "This continues to be a small number of devices overall, and we do expect more to be discovered in our investigation and via social media."

data.title: In South Korea's make-or-break college exam, even a shirt button can raise suspicion
data.description:
Key points:
  • More than half a million students sitting the crucial university entrance exam
  • Exam faces intense scrutiny after scandal over AI-assisted cheating in other key test
  • Authorities scrambled to introduce a string of new measures to deter cheating
  • Aircraft will pause take-offs for 35 minutes during English audio section

By Maggie Grether and Soohyun Jung

As South Korean students sit the country's make-or-break university entrance exam on Thursday, they have more than tough questions to worry about. They also feel they must avoid looking like cheats.

More than half a million students across the country are taking the exam, an eight-hour marathon that tests subjects from mathematics to Korean and is crucial to securing a place at a top university in the hyper-competitive country.

The exam has faced intense scrutiny this year after the top scorer in this year's national tax accountant exam admitted on Sunday to using a microcamera and an AI tool to cheat, sparking a crisis of faith in the country's test-based education system.

The scandal left authorities scrambling to introduce new measures to deter cheating, ranging from banning candidates from bringing their own pens and erasers to placing stickers on any clothing buttons that could hide microcameras.

At one test venue in the centre of Seoul, some students said the AI-cheating scandal and the new rules had made them anxious and they had changed the way they prepared for the exam.

"Now, I wonder if it would have been better to postpone the exam altogether, and come up with a proper plan," said high-school student Kwak Yoo-Min, who originally planned to wear clothes with buttons, but instead opted for a T-shirt because he was afraid of being suspected of cheating.

Jang San, another high-school student, said he hoped all candidates would take the test fairly and honestly.

The government has said it plans to tighten rules so that anyone caught cheating is banned from taking the exam for 10 years, while also facing criminal penalties.

President Lee Jae Myung called in a post on X for rewards of at least 100 million won ($75,040) for people who reported cheating attempts.

"I had worked hard and thought I was doing just as well as everyone else," said 18-year-old Jang. "But all that effort could potentially go to waste because someone uses AI just once."

At 8:30 a.m. authorities sent an emergency alert to mobile devices across the country so that they would blare at maximum volume, in a bid to detect any devices smuggled into classrooms.

The education ministry later said that authorities confiscated 22 smartphones from students at exam centres and would investigate whether they were being used for cheating.

Across South Korea, authorities take extraordinary steps to ensure those taking the papers do so under optimal conditions.

Financial markets opened an hour later on Thursday, while aircraft will not be allowed to take off for 35 minutes during the English audio section of the test to minimise distracting noise.

Police also have vehicles on standby around the country to transport students running late to test centres.

($1 = 1,332.5900 won)

data.title: Pony AI's Shares Tumble as Regulatory Environment Reassessed
data.description:
By Jiahui Huang

Pony AI's shares tumbled Thursday as investors reassessed the outlook for the robotaxi industry, and after it reported a wider loss for the third quarter .

The autonomous driving company on Wednesday reported a net loss of $105.6 million, widening from $61.3 million in the same period a year earlier, even as revenue climbed 76% to $44.6 million.

The rise in revenue was a positive for the company and the widened loss was largely on losses on traded securities, rather than operational losses. But sentiment for the stock has been hurt by as investors reevaluate risks for the industry. There are concerns that growth may be slower than hoped for, not in small part due to increased regulation and scrutiny over safety issues.

Its shares fell 9.1% to 28.90 Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to US$3.68, in early trade on Thursday .

"Although Pony AI appears on track to achieve its full-year 2026 robotaxi fleet target of 3,500 units, we see increasing downside risk to its domestic fleet expansion from 2027 onward due to a tightening of China's autonomous vehicle licensing regime," said Deutsche Bank analyst Bin Wang in a note.

After a March 2026 incident in Wuhan, where more than 100 Baidu's Apollo Go robotaxis were stalled by a system outage, China temporarily suspended new robotaxi permit approvals pending a nationwide safety review.

Approvals gradually resumed in July but the process has become more stringent, requiring municipalities to complete corrective measures and obtain sign-offs, Wang added. That is likely to delay deployments and slow fleet expansion across China's robotaxi industry, DB added.

The company's management, though, believes the regulatory environment is turning positive and recent policies are aimed at creating a standardized national framework with a uniform, high safety bar, Citi analysts wrote in a note.

This favors operators with proven technology and safety records in tier-1 cities such as Pony AI, they added.

Citi maintained its buy and high risk rating for the stock with an unchanged target price of $22.7. Deutsche Bank also maintained its buy rating but trimmed its target price to $7.00 from $14.10.

Write to Jiahui Huang at jiahui.huang@wsj.com

data.title: Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Futures Climb Ahead Of Anthropic’s Record Debut: SLS, GLD, TTWO, UNH In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The AI company also upsized its offering, selling approximately 980 million shares, bringing the amount raised to $81.3 billion. 
  • The Federal Reserve’s minutes released on Wednesday weighed on market sentiment as policymakers flagged inflation concerns and AI risks.
  • Comments from policymakers weighed on precious metals, sending gold and silver prices to their lowest levels in more than a year.

U.S. stock futures traded higher overnight late Wednesday as markets geared up for Anthropic’s public trading.

As of 10:49 p.m. EST, Dow futures climbed 0.41%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 0.63% and Nasdaq-100 futures climbed more than 1%.

On Wednesday, the three U.S. benchmark indexes closed mixed. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed more than 650 points to end the session 1.11% lower, while the S&P 500 fell 0.23%. The Nasdaq Composite closed in the green, ending the session 0.42% higher.

IndexMoveClose
Dow Jones Industrial Average-1.11%50,198.17
S&P 500-0.23%7,323.63
Nasdaq Composite0.42%24,429.88

Key US Market Drivers

This week, all eyes have been on Anthropic’s debut on stock markets, which begins trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker “ANT.”

The AI company priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above the expected range, as per a post from the company. It also upsized its offering, selling approximately 980 million shares, bringing the amount raised to $81.3 billion and surpassing SpaceX’s (SPCX) record IPO.

Ross Gerber, Co-Founder, CEO and CIO at Gerber Kawasaki, congratulated the company on its upcoming debut, saying in a post on X, “Incredible. Congrats Anthropic. Let the AI era truly begin. $ANT.”

Pro Capital (BRR) CEO Anthony Pompliano said in a post on X, “The Anthropic IPO is going to remind everyone how insane markets can be sometimes.”

The AI trade has been struggling in recent weeks amid a technology rout and a fallout in Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) dominance following CEO Jensen Huang’s infidelity reports and subsequent resignation.

“It’ll be an important barometer for investors’ AI appetite,” Callie Cox, director of investment strategy at Plancorp, said to CNBC about the IPO.

“AI stocks desperately need some wind at their backs, too ... Wall Street needs a sign that investors still believe in the potential for AI beyond already-elevated expectations,” Cox added.

Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve’s minutes released on Wednesday weighed on market sentiment as policymakers flagged inflation concerns and AI risks.

The central bank’s policymakers called artificial intelligence “a material source of inflation risk” in their latest minutes from the October meeting, adding that “off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing arrangements among AI-related firms could amplify losses if returns on AI investment were to disappoint.”

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in an interview with CNBC on Wednesday that the central bank needs to “shock people” with at least a half-percentage-point interest rate hike in the December meeting as inflationary concerns continue to mount.

A day earlier, St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said that the Federal Reserve may need several rate hikes to control inflation ​and should act soon.

Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly also noted that further interest rate hikes will be needed to ensure inflation returns to the central bank's 2% target. However, Daly suggested adopting a more “measured pace” to evaluate shifting economic conditions.

The comments sparked a selloff in markets and weighed on precious metals, sending gold and silver prices to their lowest levels in more than a year.

As per Bitcoin Archive, gold and silver’s 10% drop over the last nine days have wiped out $3.3 trillion in market value, larger than Nvidia’s over $1 trillion loss since Huang’s exit.

Meanwhile, markets will be watching out for weekly jobless claims on Thursday, and earnings from Walmart Inc. (WMT) and clothing retailer Gap Inc. (GAP).

Trending Tickers To Watch 

SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc. (SLS): The company’s shares plunged nearly 13% in the overnight session, paring phenomenal gains from Tuesday when the company revealed positive topline results for Phase 3 Regal trial of its cancer vaccine galinpepimut-S (GPS) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) after it announced a discounted public offering worth $150 million.

SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD): The gold-linked exchange-traded fund was on the retail radar amid a steep decline in the price of the yellow metal amid a rising dollar and Fed’s hawkish comments.

Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (TTWO): The gaming company’s shares surged at close and continued to climb overnight after its Grand Theft Auto VI game garnered overwhelmingly positive early reviews and its Metacritic score came in at 99 out of 100.

UnitedHealth Group Inc. (UNH): Shares of the company fell over 10% after Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed tighter Medicare and Medicaid anti-fraud audits and oversight, potentially increasing compliance and documentation requirements for managed care providers such as UnitedHealth.

Other Market Trends 

Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged higher in the overnight session.

The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was trading at 5.056%, while the 30-year yield was at 5.398%.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.19% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment.

Asian markets opened mixed on Thursday, with South Korea's KOSPI and China’s SSE Composite trading lower at the time of writing, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 was in the green. Australian stocks also traded lower at the open.

data.title: Chicago soybeans ease for fourth straight session, wheat, corn fall
data.description:
Chicago soybeans fell for a fourth straight session on Thursday, weighed down by weaker crude oil prices, which made soybean oil a less attractive biodiesel feedstock.

The most-traded soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) fell 0.29% to $12.13-1/4 a bushel at 0347 GMT.

Chicago wheat declined 0.34% to $5.84 a bushel. The contract lost 3.97% in the previous session, its biggest daily drop since September 2023.

CBOT corn fell for three straight sessions and lost 0.57% to its lowest since June 30, at $4.33 a bushel.

Brent crude oil prices fell 0.24%, making biofuels made from soybeans and corn less attractive.

US cash millfeed values were mostly steady on Wednesday, as demand in some markets helped keep a floor under prices, according to dealers

Ahead of Thursday's weekly export sales report from the US Department of Agriculture, analysts expected the government to report net export sales of US corn in the week to November 12 at 1.2 million to 2 million metric tons, wheat exports at 200,000 to 400,000 tons and soybean exports at 1 million to 2 million tons.

Recent rainfall in northeastern Brazil has kept forecasts for the country's 2026/27 soybean crop at record levels, even in a year marked by a strong El Niño, AgRural's founder said.

Farm office FranceAgriMer on Wednesday sharply raised its monthly forecast for French soft wheat exports outside the European Union this season, after demand for French supplies surged as Russia's war in Ukraine disrupted Black Sea trade.

China's corn imports in October stood at 490,000 tons, 36.8% higher than in the same period a year ago, government data showed.

data.title: Hyster-Yale Prices Upsized $135 Million Convertible Senior Notes Offering
data.description:
CLEVELAND, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyster‑Yale, Inc. () today announced the pricing of its offering of $135,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 7.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 (the "notes") in a private offering to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). The offering size was increased from the previously announced offering size of $125,000,000 aggregate principal amount of notes. The issuance and sale of the notes is scheduled to close on November 23, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Hyster‑Yale granted the initial purchasers of the notes an option to purchase, for settlement within a period of 13 days from, and including, the date the notes are first issued, up to an additional $20,000,000 aggregate principal amount of notes.

The notes will be general senior unsecured obligations of Hyster‑Yale and will accrue interest at a rate of 7.50% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on May 15 and November 15 of each year, beginning on May 15, 2027. The notes will mature on November 15, 2031, unless earlier repurchased, redeemed or converted in accordance with their terms. Before July 15, 2031, noteholders will have the right to convert their notes only upon the occurrence of certain events. At any time from, and including, July 15, 2031, noteholders may convert their notes at their election until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, irrespective of these conditions. Hyster‑Yale will settle conversions by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted and paying or delivering, as applicable, cash, shares of its Class A common stock (the "Class A common stock") or a combination of cash and shares of Class A common stock, at Hyster‑Yale's election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of its conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted. The initial conversion rate is 55.1207 shares of Class A common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which represents an initial conversion price of approximately $18.14 per share of Class A common stock. The initial conversion price represents a premium of approximately 17.5% over the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 18, 2026, which was $15.44 per share. The conversion rate will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events, but will not be adjusted for any accrued and unpaid interest.

Hyster‑Yale may not redeem the notes prior to November 20, 2029, except in the event of a cleanup redemption (as defined below). The notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part (subject to certain limitations, including a partial redemption limitation), for cash at Hyster‑Yale's option at any time, and from time to time, on a redemption date on or after November 20, 2029 and before the 61st scheduled trading day immediately prior to the maturity date, if the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock has been at least 130% of the conversion price then in effect for a specified period of time and if certain other conditions are satisfied. The redemption price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the relevant redemption date.

In addition, Hyster‑Yale may redeem for cash all, but not less than all, of the notes at any time before the 61st scheduled trading day immediately prior to the maturity date if the aggregate principal amount of the notes that remains outstanding at such time is less than 10% of the aggregate principal amount of the notes initially issued under the indenture and certain other conditions are satisfied (a "cleanup redemption"). The redemption price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the relevant redemption date.

If certain corporate events that constitute a "fundamental change" (as defined in the indenture that will govern the notes) occur, then, subject to certain conditions and exceptions, noteholders may require Hyster‑Yale to repurchase their notes for cash. The fundamental change repurchase price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the applicable fundamental change repurchase date.

Hyster‑Yale estimates that the net proceeds from the offering will be approximately $129.7 million (or approximately $149.1 million if the initial purchasers fully exercise their option to purchase additional notes), after deducting the initial purchasers' discounts and commissions and Hyster‑Yale's estimated offering expenses. Hyster‑Yale intends to use the net proceeds from the offering of the notes, together with cash on hand, (i) to repay $110.0 million of the $213.2 million principal amount outstanding under the term loan under its Amended and Restated Term Loan Credit Agreement, dated as of May 28, 2021 (the "2021 Credit Agreement"), (ii) to pay the approximately $13.5 million cost of the capped call transactions (as described below), (iii) to repurchase approximately $15 million of shares of Class A common stock concurrently with the pricing of the notes (as described below), and (iv) for general corporate purposes. If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional notes, Hyster‑Yale expects to use a portion of the net proceeds from the sale of the additional notes to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties, to repay additional principal amounts outstanding under the term loan under its 2021 Credit Agreement and, to the extent any proceeds remain, for general corporate purposes. The Company intends to repay the remaining principal amount outstanding under the term loan under its 2021 Credit Agreement on or prior to its maturity with additional long-term debt that is on terms acceptable to the Company.

Hyster‑Yale expects to use approximately $15 million of the net proceeds from the offering to repurchase approximately 971,000 shares of Class A common stock in privately negotiated transactions effected with or through one of the initial purchasers or its affiliate concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes (the "concurrent share repurchase"). The purchase price per share in the concurrent share repurchase will be $15.44 per share, which is the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on the date of the pricing of the notes. The concurrent share repurchase could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of Class A common stock, including concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes, and could have resulted in a higher effective conversion price for the notes. Hyster‑Yale cannot predict the magnitude of such market activity or the overall effect it will have on the price of the notes or the Class A common stock and the corresponding effect on the initial conversion price of the notes.

In connection with the pricing of the notes, Hyster‑Yale entered into privately negotiated capped call transactions with certain of the initial purchasers and their affiliates and certain other financial institutions (the "option counterparties"). The capped call transactions cover, subject to customary adjustments substantially similar to those applicable to the notes, the number of shares of Class A common stock initially underlying the notes. The capped call transactions are generally expected to reduce the potential dilution to the Class A common stock upon any conversion of the notes and/or offset any potential cash payments Hyster‑Yale is required to make in excess of the principal amount of such converted notes, as the case may be, with such reduction and/or offset subject to a cap based on the cap price. The cap price of the capped call transactions is initially $27.02 per share, which represents a premium of 75% over the last reported sale price per share of the Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 18, 2026 (which was $15.44 per share), and is subject to certain adjustments under the terms of the capped call transactions. If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional notes, then Hyster‑Yale expects to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties.

Hyster‑Yale has been advised that, in connection with establishing their initial hedges of the capped call transactions, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates expect to enter into various derivative transactions with respect to the Class A common stock and/or purchase shares of Class A common stock concurrently with, or shortly after, the pricing of the notes. This activity could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of the Class A common stock or the notes at that time.

In addition, Hyster-Yale has been advised that the option counterparties or their respective affiliates may modify their hedge positions by entering into or unwinding various derivatives with respect to the Class A common stock and/or purchasing or selling the Class A common stock or other securities of Hyster‑Yale in secondary market transactions following the pricing of the notes and prior to the maturity of the notes (and are likely to do so during any observation period related to a conversion of the notes, following any redemption of the notes or any repurchase of the notes upon a fundamental change, or, to the extent Hyster‑Yale exercises the relevant election under the capped call transactions, following any other repurchase of the notes). This activity could also cause or avoid an increase or a decrease in the market price of the Class A common stock or the notes, which could affect the ability of noteholders to convert the notes and, to the extent the activity occurs during any observation period related to a conversion of the notes, it could affect the number of shares of Class A common stock, if any, and value of the consideration that noteholders will receive upon conversion of the notes.

The notes are being offered only to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act. The offer and sale of the notes and any shares of Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of the notes have not been, and will not be, registered under the Securities Act or any other securities laws, and the notes and any such shares cannot be offered or sold except pursuant to an exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the registration requirements of the Securities Act and any other applicable securities laws. This press release does not constitute an offer to sell, or the solicitation of an offer to buy, the notes or any shares of Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of the notes, nor will there be any sale of the notes or any such shares, in any state or other jurisdiction in which such offer, sale or solicitation would be unlawful. This press release does not constitute an offer to buy any shares of Class A common stock in the contemplated repurchase.

data.title: Tencent Expects Lofty AI Spendings to Continue in 2027
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Tencent executives said the company's elevated artificial-intelligence spending, which has weighed on profit growth, is likely to remain near peak levels next year, while highlighting the revenue potential of its AI agent products.

Tencent has been spending heavily to build AI infrastructure, with cash capital expenditure reaching 65.1 billion yuan in the third quarter. Management said on an earnings call Thursday that AI capital spending will likely remain near current peak levels through the rest of 2026 and into 2027 before easing in 2028.

The outlook comes as investors assess whether China's leading cloud and internet companies are nearing the end of their most aggressive phase of AI investment.

Tencent has lost its position as China's most valuable company by market capitalization in recent months amid investor concerns over whether AI revenue can eventually offset the costs of building and operating the computing infrastructure needed to support the technology.

Its shares fell 6.2% in early Thursday trading amid broader technology-sector losses in Hong Kong.

Still, expectations for future spending have begun to moderate across the sector as improvements in AI model efficiency allow companies to handle more tasks with the same computing resources. Tencent has highlighted its lower-cost Hy4 Flash model as an example of how AI tasks can be processed more efficiently, reducing the need for additional hardware as usage grows.

The spending outlook also comes amid renewed U.S. efforts to restrict China's access to advanced AI chips.

Management said tighter U.S. restrictions could have a greater impact on training future generations of AI models than on its cloud services, which mainly run existing models to generate responses, a process known as inference.

"We're now at a stage where that inference can be run very effectively on a surprisingly limited number of domestic chips," Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell said.

Executives also highlighted the growing popularity of Tencent's AI workplace assistant WorkBuddy and the revenue potential of Xiaowei, an AI agent integrated into its Weixin messaging app, which is currently under beta testing.

Workbuddy has surpassed 10 million daily active users, with revenue growing more than fivefold from the previous quarter and annualized gross revenue exceeding $500 million over the past week.

Unlike consumer-facing chatbots that have struggled to convert usage into profits, WorkBuddy is designed to perform tasks such as document preparation, data analysis. Tencent President Martin Lau said 60% of China's top 100 companies have already become customers.

Tencent showcased the AI office assistant at this week's APEC summit in Shenzhen, demonstrating how it can help journalists research, write and edit stories, and even order ice cream at the venue.

The focus on WorkBuddy reflects a broader shift in investor attention from AI model capabilities to financial returns.

Management believes Xiaowei could bring AI services to a broad audience by tapping Weixin's 1.44 billion users. With Weixin already generating hundreds of billions of yuan in annual revenue, the AI agent could potentially boost that figure by another 10%-20%, Lau said.

That "will make Xiaowei hugely profitable for us," Lau said, adding that its revenue potential should become clearer over the next six to 12 months.

"Management's candid tone on earnings call should help address investor concerns on chip restriction and future monetization potential for WorkBuddy and Weixin Xiaowei," Citi analysts said in a note.

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com

data.title: BOJ's Ueda Vows to Keep Careful Eye on Fed Moves — Update
data.description:
By Megumi Fujikawa

TOKYO--Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda pledged to closely watch how Federal Reserve policy changes affect growth and inflation in Japan, while reaffirming his readiness to keep tightening monetary settings.

"With the Fed raising interest rates and many other central banks pivoting toward hikes, we need to carefully monitor how those rate moves and the accompanying changes in global financial conditions affect Japan's economy and prices," Ueda told a parliamentary committee on Thursday.

Ueda noted that currency fluctuations--which can be heavily swayed by Fed policy--are more likely to affect domestic prices than in the past as companies in Japan become more comfortable passing on costs to consumers.

"We will conduct monetary policy appropriately while keeping in mind that these shifts could in turn influence underlying inflation through changes in inflation expectations," he added.

While BOJ policymakers are cautious about cooling the economy with monetary tightening, further action looks necessary to keep inflation in check, especially as heightened expectations for Fed rate hikes pressure the yen.

Market participants see a growing chance that the BOJ could raise rates again as soon as December. The Fed is also widely expected to hike next month as U.S. inflation continues to concern officials.

The BOJ is keeping an eye on inflation too. Ueda again stressed the importance of anchoring underlying consumer inflation around 2% so it doesn't overshoot the central bank's target and hurt the economy.

He warned that one measure of underlying inflation--consumer prices excluding fresh food--is likely to accelerate clearly above 2% as firms pass on higher labor costs, oil remains expensive and yen weakness persists. Surging global demand related to the artificial-intelligence buildout adds another inflationary impulse.

In September, that gauge of underlying inflation accelerated to 2.1% year-on-year from August's 1.7%. Economists polled by data provider Quick expect October figures due Friday to show a further rise to 2.3%.

The BOJ said last month that underlying inflation had reached its 2% target for the first time since the goal was introduced in 2013. It held policy settings steady at its previous meeting in October after raising rates to 1.25% in September.

Despite the rate hikes delivered so far, the BOJ governor still sees Japan's financial conditions as accommodative, although he acknowledged that monetary tightening is affecting households and businesses through higher mortgage rates and funding costs.

"The bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation, in response to developments in economic activity and prices as well as financial conditions," he said.

Write to Megumi Fujikawa at megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com

data.title: MCX share price target raised by UBS backing strong volume growth
data.description:
Shares of Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) Ltd. declined on Thursday, November 19, even as global investment banking firm UBS reiterated its positive stance and raised its target price on the stock by 18%.

UBS has a "buy" recommendation on MCX and has raised its target price to ₹4,500 from the previous ₹3,800 apiece. This indicates an upside of 24.3% from its previous closing price.

UBS said MCX has improving volume resilience and the potential for its trading activity to sustain at a higher base. Since then, the trading activity has strengthened further in the third quarter of this fiscal, reinforcing the view that the exchange is operating at a structurally-higher activity base, it said.

MCX's average daily transaction free revenue has reached ₹12,700 crore in the third quarter, so far compared to ₹10,900 crore in the previous quarter, with the November month-to-date (MTD) has reached ₹14,300 crore.

At the current volume run rate, the annualized earnings per share (EPS) would be ₹10,000 crore, 15% above the estimated FY28 EPS of ₹87, suggesting further upside, UBS said.

It added that participation has also broadened significantly, with F&O traded clients nearly doubling to 1.5 million in the second quarter from the previous year.

As a result, UBS has raised its EPS estimates for MCX by 4%, 8% and 13% for financial year 2027, 2028 and 2029 respectively.

Of the 17 analysts who have coverage on the stock, 16 have a "buy" rating and one has a "hold" recommendation. The consensus estimates of price targets implies an upside potential of 8.6% from current levels.

Shares of MCX are trading 2.2% lower on Thursday, at ₹3,540.6. The stock is still up 11% over the last one month, taking its year-to-date advance to 62%.

data.title: Fairfax likely buyer in IIFL Capital's $165 million block deal, CNBC-TV18 reports
data.description:
Shares worth 15.40 billion rupees ($164.8 million) in India's IIFL Capital changed hands in a block deal on Thursday, according to exchange data.

Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings was the likely buyer, CNBC-TV18 reported, citing sources.

IIFL Capital and Fairfax did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

The transaction comes a day after Fairfax sold its entire stake in IIFL Finance , a move Reuters had reported was aimed at unlocking funds for its acquisition of a 60% stake in IDBI Bank from the Indian government and state-owned insurer Life Insurance Corp of India.

The IDBI Bank deal, valued at 528.78 billion rupees ($5.66 billion), ranks among the largest cross-border transactions in India's banking sector.

Fairfax currently owns 38.05% of IIFL Capital Services, which operates investment banking and wealth management businesses, and has previously said it intends to raise its stake to 51%.

The Canadian investor also owns 49% of insurer Digit and plans to consolidate its Indian investments across insurance, investment banking and wealth management under IDBI Bank, creating a diversified financial services group.

data.title: Anthropic, Nvidia And The Next AI Trade: Michael Burry Explains What Could Break The Bull Case
data.description:
Key points:
  • Burry said he may let AI stocks run before shorting them, citing bear market rallies that averaged 22% in the 1930s and 2000s.
  • He sees a threat to Anthropic and Nvidia as businesses build smaller AI models that run on their own machines.
  • Tencent’s 69.1 billion yuan cash burn kept Burry from adding shares. He also thinks private credit buyers may be early.

As Anthropic prepares to go public, “The Big Short” investor Michael Burry sees a rally he might eventually short and also detailed in Nvidia’s earnings he couldn’t overlook: the chipmaker was waiting longer to get paid.

“It is pumping futures for now,” Burry said in his Substack chat when a reader asked about the IPO. Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 apiece, above its proposed $70 to $78 range, ahead of Thursday’s expected Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT.

Burry had already said he would pass on the offering and on buying shares afterward. He put Anthropic’s commitments at more than $1 trillion and questioned whether revenue could grow fast enough to cover them.

Why Burry Might Let AI Stocks Run

When asked whether to buy AI stocks through year-end or sell into a rebound, Burry said he was willing to wait for a better entry on the bearish side. “I cannot give advice but I will look to short on any rip, though I may let it run for a bit; the average bear market rally in both the 1930s and the 2000s was 22%,” he said.

He had made a similar trade last week, doubling his Nasdaq-100 put position when the index bounced from around 27,000. He also bought back some puts on the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) after trimming the bet.

The 4 Extra Days That Caught Burry’s Eye At NVDA

Burry went into Nvidia’s (NVDA) earnings holding $140 puts expiring in February 2027 and passed on buying short-dated calls to cushion the bet. After the results, he said he planned to spend less time covering Nvidia, but one number stood out.

Days sales outstanding, a measure of how long it takes to collect payment, rose to 64 days from 60. Customers owed Nvidia $81 billion at quarter-end, as quarterly revenue more than doubled from a year earlier to $115.8 billion.

“Without Jensen there I wonder how this improves - customers will find it harder to pay, or will just take more time to pay, I imagine,” Burry said, referring to former CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia attributed the increase to the timing of Rubin chip shipments and longer payment terms for some investment-grade customers.

Burry also flagged the wait for Nvidia’s 10-Q, which interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said would arrive in the coming weeks. When a reader questioned why the earnings call lasted just 48 minutes including Q&A, Burry replied, “Earnings calls are controlled environments, and with over 70 sell side analysts covering it, clearly this was invitation only with some instruction.”

When asked how much weight to give the SEC investigation into Nvidia, Burry said, “The SEC just doesn't have the resources or ability to do much.”

Burry Sees A Threat To Anthropic And Nvidia 

A reader who identified themselves as a law firm owner challenged Burry to give an AI agent five years of company filings and ask it to flag changes in depreciation assumptions, down to the exact footnotes.

“As a business owner, I know what an afternoon of my team’s time is worth. Give me that afternoon back every week and I’ll gladly write that check every month,” the reader said.

Burry agreed that kind of tool was coming. He said that businesses could run smaller models on their own machines, using their own records. He said rising costs in China showed how expensive inference (the work a model does to answer a question) could become in the U.S. He also pointed to compression as a way to fit models onto smaller devices.

“I know of people creating their own SLMs inside their homes with AI servers in house. This works against the Anthropic model and the Nvidia model. Brute force and mass resource usage is not the way forward,” he said, referring to small language models.

Nvidia already makes hardware for the market. Its Nemotron 3.5 Bolt model can run on GeForce RTX graphics cards.

Tencent’s Cash Burn Gives Burry A Reason To Wait

Meanwhile, Tencent accounted for just over 2% of Burry’s portfolio earlier this month. The company subsequently reported negative quarterly free cash flow of 69.1 billion yuan.

“It is concerning and the main reason I have not added. I am not sure, if AI bulls are correct, when the hyperscaler spending actually stops or is reduced,” Burry said, referring to spending by the biggest cloud computing companies.

He also questioned whether bargain hunters in private credit were moving too soon. “I've heard capital is already being mobilized to pick at depressed private credit. Could be a self-fulfilling prophecy, but if the size of the AI boom's bust is large enough at the data center level, moves today would likely be overwhelmed and proven early,” he said.

Why Burry Cut His NFLX Target And Stuck With ERO

Burry also explained why his buy target for Netflix (NFLX) had fallen to the high $30s. In July, he had put the low $50s just outside his buying range and questioned the staying power of its hits. “Disney produces wine. Netflix produces milk,” he said at the time.

In the latest chat, Burry said streaming rivals had caught up. “The process of producing hit shows has been a fraught exercise for a long time, and reality TV is a sign of rot in that creative process. It is the cheap more certain option, but one that does not breed network loyalty,” he said.

Burry was equally open about Ero Copper (ERO). In September, he saw a mismatch that favored the miner. Data centers could lift copper demand within two or three years, while new deposits could take about 18 years to reach production.

“My investment in ERO was ill-timed. I still own it in small size but have not added but once,” he said in the latest chat. “I will continue to evaluate it but I think this one has more to it than the AI trade. As I said it is not often I get bullish on a miner.”

data.title: Automakers seek EV-like credits for plug-in hybrids to ease tougher emission norms
data.description:
Automakers are preparing to seek the same regulatory benefits for plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) as fully electric vehicles (EVs) under the upcoming Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFÉ)-III norms, a move that could help manufacturers with large petrol and diesel SUV portfolios meet tighter fleet-level fuel-efficiency requirements.

JSW MG Motor, which has introduced a locally manufactured plug-in hybrid, could be among the immediate beneficiaries. BYD and Stellantis, which are evaluating or planning plug-in hybrid models for India, could also gain if their proposed products reach the market.

The CAFÉ-III norms will come into effect on April 1, 2027, and remain applicable until March 31, 2032. Under the proposed framework, EVs and range-extender electric vehicles (REEVs) receive the highest super-credit multiplier of 3, compared with 2.5 for PHEVs and 1.6 for strong hybrids.

Automakers want PHEVs placed in the same regulatory category as EVs and REEVs, arguing that plug-in hybrids can operate entirely on electric power for shorter journeys despite also having an internal combustion engine.

“In some large auto markets of the world, PHEV is viewed as EV since it can run purely on electric propulsion just like an EV. That is why we are hoping that PHEVs can be seen in the same bracket as EV and REEV,” a senior official at a passenger vehicle manufacturer told Moneycontrol, requesting anonymity as the discussions are still private.

The official said the industry has not yet approached the government but plans to submit its proposal soon.

Who could benefit?

JSW MG Motor is among the clearest potential beneficiaries, having introduced the seven-seater Hector Tomahawk in August 2026, making it the first locally manufactured PHEV in India's mass-market passenger vehicle segment.

The company has already sought more favourable taxation for plug-in hybrids. In August, JSW MG Motor director Parth Jindal said the 40 percent GST rate constrained the company's ability to price the technology competitively.

The Hector Tomahawk PHEV was priced at Rs 25.69 lakh, compared with Rs 19.49 lakh for its electric counterpart, highlighting the pricing challenge facing the technology.

BYD could also benefit as it evaluates plug-in hybrids for India. The Chinese automaker, which has an extensive international PHEV portfolio, has conducted local testing but has yet to finalise the models or their launch timeline.

Stellantis, which operates the Jeep and Citroën brands in India, has included PHEVs in its future product strategy. In October, the company outlined plans for 12 products and upgrades over three years, including vehicles using hybrid, plug-in hybrid and electric powertrains.

Luxury automakers such as Mercedes-Benz and BMW, which already sell plug-in hybrids in India, could also benefit from a higher multiplier, although the impact would depend on their sales volumes and overall fleet composition.

Maruti Suzuki and Toyota, which have invested heavily in hybrid technology, could be potential beneficiaries if they introduce qualifying PHEVs. Their existing strong-hybrid models fall in a separate regulatory category and would not automatically qualify for the proposed higher PHEV credits.

Similarly, manufacturers with large petrol and diesel SUV portfolios, including Mahindra and Tata Motors, could benefit from greater regulatory flexibility if they add PHEVs to their product line-ups. Their existing fully electric models already qualify for the highest multiplier.

There is, however, no confirmation that these manufacturers are individually backing the proposed change. Their potential benefits are based on their existing products, announced strategies and fleet composition.

Compliance challenge

Super credits are important because CAFÉ norms assess a manufacturer's sales-weighted fleet average rather than the emissions or fuel consumption of individual models.

Under the proposed framework, higher multipliers allow qualifying lower-emission vehicles to carry greater weight in compliance calculations, helping manufacturers offset the impact of conventional petrol and diesel models.

This is particularly relevant for automakers with significant SUV sales, since larger and heavier vehicles generally consume more fuel and make fleet-level targets harder to achieve.

Raising the PHEV multiplier from 2.5 to 3 would increase the regulatory benefit of selling such vehicles. The actual advantage would depend on PHEV sales volumes, their certified fuel consumption and the composition of each manufacturer's overall portfolio.

Automakers are also looking at international regulatory practices to support their case.

China classifies EVs, REEVs and PHEVs within its broader new energy vehicle category. In the United States, PHEVs receive partial zero-emission vehicle credits based on their electric driving capability, while range-extender vehicles are generally treated within the PHEV framework.

However, the regulatory treatment of these technologies differs across markets, and their inclusion in a common category does not necessarily mean they receive identical compliance benefits.

India has 13 PHEVs on sale, according to industry estimates cited in the original reporting, but only one is in the non-luxury segment. The remaining models are offered by premium and luxury manufacturers, including Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Ferrari and Lamborghini.

PHEVs combine an internal combustion engine with a rechargeable battery that can be charged externally, much like an EV.

While pure EVs typically offer more than 300 km of electric driving range, PHEVs generally provide around 80–120 km of electric-only driving before relying on their combustion engines for longer journeys. Their batteries can also recover energy through regenerative braking.

The technology therefore offers a middle ground between conventional hybrids and fully electric vehicles, although its real-world fuel consumption and emissions depend significantly on how frequently the battery is charged and how the vehicle is driven.

Taxation is another challenge.

EVs and hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles attract GST of 5 percent, while other vehicle technologies are subject to higher rates of 18 percent or 40 percent, depending on classification. Strong hybrids, including the Maruti Suzuki Grand Vitara, Toyota Innova Hycross and Toyota Urban Cruiser Hyryder, fall under the 40 percent bracket.

A higher CAFÉ-III multiplier would not change the GST treatment of PHEVs but could provide manufacturers with an additional incentive to introduce them.

For automakers, the proposed change could offer a way to balance continued demand for petrol and diesel SUVs with increasingly stringent fuel-efficiency requirements. Whether the government accepts the industry's argument will determine how much regulatory support plug-in hybrids receive under India's next phase of emission-related standards.
